newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo wins almost one bln rand from hedging.
newsitem.headline: Anglo wins almost one bln rand from hedging.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, detailing hedges in place, said on Thursday that its gold hedging programme had earned it between 800 million and one billion rand over the last six years.

Anglo's gold and uranium division -- renamed Anglogold -- marketing director Kelvin Williams said at the company's third quarter gold results presentation that by hedging, Anglo had been able to continue production in certain area which could have been threatened by rising costs.
"We are not only a billion rand ahead, 500 million of that we made in the early nineties," he told Reuters later and added that Anglogold believed its hedging policy to be satisfactory.
"The overall results of this hedging policy have been satisfactory for us and for some six years we have reported prices on average higher than the industry received gold price," Williams said.
Anglo's policy was to sell forward a percentage of its projected production.
"We have attempted to secure in these hedges the highest level of price security for the lowest level of cost in terms of price upside.

"The hedges in place in our books consist of both rand gold and dollar gold priced spot deferred contracts and forward contracts, as well as put and call options priced in both rand gold and in dollar gold," Williams said.

A portion of these forward sales consists of dollar priced contracts which have been converted to rand prices at average annual forward rand values based on a spot rand/dollar exchange rate of 4.53 available on September 30,1996.
Anglogold on Thursday detailed its existing forward sales commitments.
